Fixed edit-employee prefill. Several issues were preventing saved data from showing correctly.

### Root causes
1. **Hydration ran only once** — After the first load, the form ignored fresher API data (e.g. when the employee record finished loading).

3. **Lookup IDs** — Some API responses expose IDs on nested objects (`role.id`) rather than scalar `roleId` fields.
4. **Empty dropdowns** — Selects looked blank when the saved ID wasn’t in the lookups list yet (or the option was inactive).
5. **Visa auto-fill** — Changing visa type on load could overwrite saved contracted hours.

### Fixes
- **`mapEmployeeDetailToFormValues`** — Maps personal and employment independently; resolves IDs from scalars or nested relations; handles numeric hour fields reliably.
- **Re-hydrate when API data updates** — Uses `dataUpdatedAt` so the form resets when the server payload changes.
- **`LookupSelect`** — Shows a saved label when the value isn’t in the current options list.
- **Visa hours** — Only auto-fills contracted hours when the user changes visa type, not on initial load.
- **Backend** — `GET /employees/:id` now includes `location` and `baseLocation` on employment for labels.

Here is an analysis of what your app already stores for a service user, plus a **copy-paste prompt for Claude** to design the dashboard UI.

---

## What exists today

**Route:** `/service-users/:serviceUserId/view` → `ViewServiceUserPage` (basic dashboard)

**Already loaded on dashboard:**
- Profile (name, DOB, photo, risk level, care type, status, NHS number, funding)
- Flash message (urgent handover-style alert)
- Documents summary (DNACPR, LPA health/finance, DoLS certificates)
- Allergies count, inventory count, contacts count
- Initial assessment summary (carers planned, on-file flag)

**Separate module pages** (icon tabs: Observations, Care Plan, Meds, Body Map; Comms/History/Alerts coming soon):

| Module | Data / actions |
|--------|----------------|
| **Edit profile** | Personal details, contacts/family, About Me, photos, inventory, allergies, documents, absences, calendar, privacy, DOM care, enterprise initial assessment, funding, live-in profile |
| **Care plan** | Accepted care plans, form catalogue, review summary, assessment, risk profile, body map link, care actions/history, consent & capacity |
| **Medication** | MAR records, support profile, calendar, supply/cycles, blister packs, events, activity log, review queue, export |
| **Observations** | Clinical observations (NEWS2, fluids, seizures, ABC, urinalysis, infections), wellbeing radar chart |
| **Body map** | Wounds, pressure, medication sites, safeguarding, alerts, handover, standing/leaning/sitting diagrams |
| **Calendar** | Service user events / visits |

**Key profile fields** (`ServiceUserDetail`): service user number, resident IDs, names, DOB, contact info, NHS/social services/NI numbers, service start/end dates, title/gender/marital status, status, care type, funding type, risk level (with color), location, key worker, named nurse, address (with access/key safe), contacts, references, assignment history.

**List-level flags:** active absence, active flash message.

**Design patterns in app:** teal primary (`teal-800`), card + teal header strips on current dashboard, `GeneralSettingsPage`-style sidebar for care plan form, module header with circular photo + DNACPR/diabetes badges, Figma icon module tabs, `max-w-7xl` content width, light/dark support.

---

## Prompt for Claude (copy everything below)

```markdown
# Design brief: Service User Dashboard UI (CareAdmin — UK social care)

You are designing a **high-fidelity UI/UX** for a **Service User Dashboard** in **CareAdmin**, a web admin app for UK domiciliary and residential care providers (CQC-aligned workflows). The dashboard is the **single landing page** when staff open one service user — it must answer: *Who is this person? What needs attention today? Where do I go next?*

Deliver: **(1)** information architecture, **(2)** desktop wireframe (1440px) + mobile notes (375px), **(3)** component breakdown with states (loading, empty, error, alerts), **(4)** colour/typography tied to spec below. Use **React + Tailwind** mental model. No backend code — UI only.

---

## Product context

- **Users:** care coordinators, nurses, managers, admin staff (desktop-first, tablet second).
- **Regulatory tone:** clinical clarity, audit-friendly, no playful consumer-app aesthetics.
- **Existing route:** `/service-users/{id}/view` — replace/enhance the current grid of teal-header cards.
- **Navigation:** Dashboard is **hub**; deep work happens in modules (edit profile, care plan, meds, observations, body map, calendar).

---

## Design system (match existing CareAdmin)

- **Primary brand:** teal (`#115E59` / `teal-800` headers, `teal-700` links).
- **Destructive / clinical emphasis:** red for DOB line, overdue meds, high risk.
- **Surfaces:** `bg-card`, `border-border`, `bg-muted/20` page background, `rounded-xl` panels, subtle shadows.
- **Layout width:** `max-w-7xl` centered; sticky top **identity bar** + optional **module shortcut strip** below.
- **Patterns to reuse:**
  - **Settings-style sidebar** for dense sub-sections (vertical nav, active left border) — reference General Settings.
  - **Module tabs:** circular icon + label (Observations, Comms, Care Plan, Meds, History, Body Map, Alerts) — some disabled “coming soon”.
  - **Flash message:** amber banner, lightning icon, “until {date}” — highest priority alert.
- **Accessibility:** WCAG AA contrast, focus rings, icon+text labels, don’t rely on colour alone for risk.

---

## Identity header (always visible)

**Left:**
- Profile photo (96px circle) or “NO IMAGE” placeholder
- Full name (preferred name if set)
- **DOB** (prominent, red/destructive tone — safety critical)
- Service user number `#12345`
- Badges: **Risk level** (colour from API), **Care type**, **Status** (Active/Inactive/etc.)

**Right — quick actions:**
- “Service user tasks” → calendar
- “Service users” → list
- “Calendar”
- **Edit profile** (primary CTA, teal button)
- Optional overflow: print summary, add flash message

**Under header (if active):**
- **Flash message** full-width amber alert OR dashed “No active flash message”

**Clinical chips row (from modules):**
- DNACPR in place (yes/no)
- Diabetes allergy flag
- Active absence today
- Open body-map alerts count
- MAR reviews overdue count (if any)
- Care plan publish status (draft / published)

---

## Dashboard body — recommended layout

### Option A (preferred): **Bento grid + attention column**

**Row 1 — “Needs attention today” (full width or 2/3)**
Horizontal **alert cards** (only if data exists; hide section if empty):
- Flash message (duplicate mini if not in header)
- Body map: reviews due / safeguarding
- Medication: missed or review-queue items
- Observations: abnormal NEWS2 or fluid balance flag
- Initial assessment: submission awaiting review
- Absence: currently away (dates)
- Care plan: unpublished / review overdue

Each card: severity colour left border, title, 1-line detail, **Open →** deep link.

**Row 2 — three columns (desktop) / stack (mobile)**

| Column 1 — **Care overview** | Column 2 — **Clinical & safety** | Column 3 — **People & admin** |
|------------------------------|-----------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Care plan status (count accepted, last review date) | Allergies (count + top 3 names) | Key worker + named nurse (avatars/initials) |
| Visit schedule snippet (next 3 visits) | Risk level + summary | Location / address snippet |
| DOM care / live-in indicator | Body map: active records by type | Funding type + primary package |
| Initial assessment status | Documents: DNACPR, LPA, DoLS checklist | Contacts: primary + emergency count |

**Row 3 — **Module launcher****
Grid of **large tiles** (icon, title, subtitle, badge count):
- Observations
- Care Plan
- Medication (MAR)
- Body Map
- Edit profile (or split “Profile” vs “Documents”)
- Calendar
- Initial Assessment (deep link to edit tab)
- Comms / History / Alerts (disabled, “Coming soon”)

**Row 4 — **Recent activity timeline**** (optional v2)
Last 5–8 events: med administered, observation logged, body map update, care plan published — timestamp + actor + link.

---

## Data available from API (design realistic widgets)

### Core profile (`GET /service-users/:id`)
- Names, DOB, email, phone, mobile, NHS number, social services ref, NI number
- Service start/end, notes, isActive
- Lookups: title, gender, marital status, status, care type, funding type, risk level (+ colour)
- Location, key worker, named nurse (employee names)
- Address: lines, postcode, access instructions, key safe
- Contacts[]: name, relationship, phone, primary/emergency flags
- References[], assignment history

### Parallel dashboard fetches (already used on view page)
- **Documents:** legal DNACPR (in place + certificate URL), LPA health/finance certs, DoLS rows (current/past, dates, certificate links)
- **Allergies:** list with names/severity
- **Inventory:** personal items count
- **Initial assessment:** on file yes/no, `numberOfCarers` planned
- **Flash message:** message text, `displayUntil` date, active flag

### Modules (link out; show summary counts on dashboard)
- **Care plans:** accepted plans, draft vs published, recommendations from IA
- **Medications:** active meds, blister packs, review queue, late doses
- **Observations:** recent by type, wellbeing radar average, fluid balance
- **Body map:** summary — open wounds, pressure areas, medication sites, alerts[], handover preview
- **Calendar:** upcoming visits/events
- **Funding:** enterprise funding rows (status, weekly budget, funder, review date)
- **Absences:** active span, reason
- **DOM care:** package/visit pattern flags

---

## States to design

1. **Loading:** skeleton for header + 6 cards + module tiles
2. **Error:** banner + retry; keep header if cached
3. **Empty service user:** rare — redirect message
4. **Partial data:** cards show “Not recorded” / “—” without breaking layout
5. **High-risk user:** risk badge + optional subtle page tint or top border (not alarming red wash)

---

## Interactions

- Click card → navigate to correct module/tab (e.g. Documents → edit `?tab=documents`, Care plan → `/care-plan`, Meds → `/medication?view=reviews`)
- Flash section: `?focus=flash` scroll target (keep)
- Module tiles: same routes as `ServiceUserModuleTabs`
- **Do not** embed full MAR or care plan forms on dashboard — summaries only

---

## Out of scope for v1 UI

- Family portal
- Billing/invoicing
- Staff roster editing
- Full calendar month view (link only)

---

## Deliverables checklist

1. One-page **IA diagram** (sections + links)
2. **Desktop wireframe** (Figma-style description or ASCII + annotations)
3. **Mobile adaptation** (stack order, which cards collapse)
4. **Component list:** `DashboardIdentityHeader`, `AttentionStrip`, `SummaryCard`, `ModuleTile`, `ActivityTimelineItem`
5. **Sample copy** for empty states and alert severities (UK English)
6. **Rationale** (2–3 paragraphs): why bento + attention-first fits care workers

---

## Reference: current implementation (weaknesses to improve)

Today the view page is a **static 3-column grid** of teal-header cards (Personal, Assessments, Documents, Care plan placeholder, Visits placeholder, Conditions, Risk) with many “Further modules will appear” notes. Your design should **replace placeholders with real summary widgets** and **surface actionable alerts**, while feeling cohesive with teal branding and the newer sidebar-nav patterns used elsewhere in the app.

---

## Tone & copy examples

- “3 allergies recorded — includes diabetes”
- “Care plan not published — implement after publish”
- “2 body map reviews due this week”
- “Initial assessment complete · 2 carers planned”
- “Absent until 12 Jun 2026 — family holiday”

Design for **scanability in under 10 seconds** for a nurse starting a shift.
```

---

## How to use this with Claude

1. Paste the full block above into Claude (Artifacts or Projects work well for wireframes).
2. Optionally attach a screenshot of `ViewServiceUserPage` and `GeneralSettingsPage` sidebar.
3. Ask for iteration: e.g. “Add a compact mode for ward managers viewing 20 users” or “Produce Figma component specs.”

If you want this implemented in `care-admin` next (replacing `ViewServiceUserPage`), say so and we can build it against real API summary endpoints.

  "contents": "import type { PhotonFeature } from '@/shared/lib/osm-photon'

export type ParsedPostalAddress = {
  addressLine1: string
  addressLine2: string
  town: string
  county: string
  country: string
  postcode: string
  latitude: number | null
  longitude: number | null
  formattedAddress: string
}

/** Map a Photon (OSM) result to CareAdmin address fields. */
export function parsePhotonFeature(feature: PhotonFeature): ParsedPostalAddress {
  const p = feature.properties
  const [lng, lat] = feature.geometry.coordinates

  const streetLine = [p.housenumber, p.street].filter(Boolean).join(' ').trim()
  const addressLine1 = streetLine || p.name?.trim() || ''
  const addressLine2 = streetLine && p.name && p.name !== streetLine ? p.name : ''

  const town = p.city?.trim() || p.district?.trim() || ''
  const county = p.state?.trim() || ''
  const country = p.country?.trim() || ''
  const postcode = p.postcode?.trim() || ''

  const formattedAddress = [addressLine1, addressLine2, town, county, postcode, country]
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join(', ')

  return {
    addressLine1,
    addressLine2,
    town,
    county,
    country,
    postcode,
    latitude: Number.isFinite(lat) ? lat : null,
    longitude: Number.isFinite(lng) ? lng : null,
    formattedAddress: formattedAddress || addressLine1,
  }
}

export function formatAddressLines(value: {
  addressLine1?: string
  addressLine2?: string
  town?: string
  county?: string
  country?: string
  postcode?: string
}): string {
  return [
    value.addressLine1,
    value.addressLine2,
    value.town,
    value.county,
    value.postcode,
    value.country,
  ]
    .map((s) => s?.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join(', ')
}
"
}

Time slots are now driven from the database end to end.

### Why it looked hardcoded before
The Add medication dialog was using **static labels** (Morning, Midday, etc.) and only inferring the slot from the time picker. The data was already in the DB (`MedicationAdministrationRound`), but the UI didn’t let you **pick** a slot from that list.

- **Edit** existing slots (already supported; unchanged)  
- New slots are saved to `MedicationAdministrationRound` via `POST /medication-administration-rounds`

**2. Add medication dialog**  
- Each row has a **Time slot** dropdown loaded from `medication-lookups` rounds (same catalogue as MAR)  
- Choosing a slot fills the **due time** from the database  
- **Custom time** is still available if needed  
- Already-used slots are disabled in the dropdown to avoid duplicates  
- “Add time” picks the next unused slot from settings  

**3. Data flow**

```
Settings → Medication  →  DB (MedicationAdministrationRound)
                              ↓
                    GET /medication-lookups/rounds
                              ↓
              Add medication → Time slot dropdown
```

### Where to configure slots
Go to **Settings → Medication** → **Time slots**.  
Default slots (Morning → Night) come from seed data; you can add more (e.g. Breakfast) there and they appear in Add medication after a refresh.

If your dropdown is empty, run the backend seed so the default five slots exist, or add slots manually in Settings.

import {
  normalizeDueTimeHm,
  sortMedicationRounds,
  type MedicationRoundLookup,
} from '@/features/service-users/medication/medication-time-slots'
import type { VisitPlanSlot } from '@/features/service-users/visit-plan/types'

const SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS: Omit<
  VisitPlanSlot,
  | 'slotCode'
  | 'label'
  | 'daysOfWeek'
  | 'plannedStartTime'
  | 'plannedEndTime'
  | 'requiredCarers'
  | 'isEnabled'

  scheduleFrequency: 'DAILY',
  repeatEvery: 1,
  repeatUnit: 'DAYS',
  timeCritical: false,
  timeToleranceMinutes: 30,
  durationMinutes: null,
  notesRequired: false,
  photoAllowed: false,
  shareOutcomeWithFamily: false,
  analysisArea: null,
  monthlyDayMode: 'BY_DATE',
  monthlyDaysOfMonth: [],
  monthlyPatternOrdinal: 'FIRST',
  monthlyPatternWeekday: 1,
  linkedCarePlanFormIds: [],
  assignedEmployeeIds: [],
}

const LEGACY_SLOT_TO_ROUND: Record<string, string> = {
  LUNCH: 'MIDDAY',
  TEA: 'AFTERNOON',
}

export function normalizeVisitPlanSlotCode(code: string): string {
  const upper = code.trim().toUpperCase()
  return LEGACY_SLOT_TO_ROUND[upper] ?? upper
}

function hm(value: string | null | undefined, fallback: string): string {
  return normalizeDueTimeHm(value) ?? fallback
}

type RoundInput = MedicationRoundLookup | MedicationRoundRow

function toRoundLookup(rounds: RoundInput[]): MedicationRoundLookup[] {
  return rounds.map(r => ({
    id: 'id' in r ? r.id : r.code,
    name: r.name,
    code: r.code,
    time: r.time,
    windowStart: r.windowStart,
    windowEnd: r.windowEnd,
    sortOrder: r.sortOrder,
  }))
}

export function visitPlanSlotsFromMedicationRounds(
  rounds: RoundInput[],
  existing?: VisitPlanSlot[],
): VisitPlanSlot[] {
  const sorted = sortMedicationRounds(toRoundLookup(rounds))
  const byCode = new Map(
    (existing ?? []).map(slot => [normalizeVisitPlanSlotCode(slot.slotCode), slot]),
  )

  return sorted.map((round, index) => {
    const slotCode = round.code
    const prev = byCode.get(slotCode)
    const start = hm(round.windowStart, hm(round.time, '08:00'))
    const end = hm(round.windowEnd, hm(round.time, '09:00'))

    return {
      id: prev?.id,
      slotCode,
      label: round.name,
      medicationRoundCode: round.code,
      daysOfWeek: prev?.daysOfWeek ?? [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 0],
      plannedStartTime: prev?.plannedStartTime ?? start,
      plannedEndTime: prev?.plannedEndTime ?? end,
      requiredCarers: prev?.requiredCarers ?? 1,
      isEnabled: prev?.isEnabled ?? false,
      notes: prev?.notes ?? '',
      sortOrder: round.sortOrder ?? index,
      scheduleFrequency: prev?.scheduleFrequency ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.scheduleFrequency,
      repeatEvery: prev?.repeatEvery ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.repeatEvery,
      repeatUnit: prev?.repeatUnit ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.repeatUnit,
      timeCritical: prev?.timeCritical ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.timeCritical,
      timeToleranceMinutes: prev?.timeToleranceMinutes ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.timeToleranceMinutes,
      durationMinutes: prev?.durationMinutes ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.durationMinutes,
      notesRequired: prev?.notesRequired ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.notesRequired,
      photoAllowed: prev?.photoAllowed ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.photoAllowed,
      shareOutcomeWithFamily:
        prev?.shareOutcomeWithFamily ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.shareOutcomeWithFamily,
      analysisArea: prev?.analysisArea ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.analysisArea,
      monthlyDayMode: prev?.monthlyDayMode ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.monthlyDayMode,
      monthlyDaysOfMonth: prev?.monthlyDaysOfMonth ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.monthlyDaysOfMonth,
      monthlyPatternOrdinal:
        prev?.monthlyPatternOrdinal ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.monthlyPatternOrdinal,
      monthlyPatternWeekday:
        prev?.monthlyPatternWeekday ?? SLOT_OPTION_DEFAULTS.monthlyPatternWeekday,
      linkedCarePlanFormIds: prev?.linkedCarePlanFormIds ?? [],
      assignedEmployeeIds: prev?.assignedEmployeeIds ?? [],
    }
  })
}

export function defaultEditableVisitPlanSlots(rounds: RoundInput[]): VisitPlanSlot[] {
  return visitPlanSlotsFromMedicationRounds(rounds)
}
